correctness.rationale: Gaussian sign covariance and the Brownian occupation covariance yield exact estimator and risk. Direct elementary integration gives F; F is strictly concave for all finite relative noise, its derivative diverges positively at x down to zero and is strictly negative at x=1. Hence the unique critical point is a global maximum. Substitution gives exact optimizer and risk and elementary Taylor expansion gives high-noise laws. Reproducibility checks confirm identities but are not treated as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: A complete closed-form design for an information-constrained natural occupation integral, with one bit per path and all finite relative-noise levels, gives a principled measurement time, exact Bayes risk and large-noise transition, not a mere change of notation or a known-table recomputation. At zero prequantization noise one bit retains 66.39% of occupation variance, a meaningful baseline for low-bandwidth path sensing. This does not claim a general optimal quantizer.
